title: Bug: `test_intf_fec.py` fails with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''`
author: arista-nwolfe
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

```
        for intf in intf_status:
            intf_name = intf['iface']
            speed = duthost.get_speed(intf_name)
            # Convert the speed to gbps format
>           speed_gbps = f"{int(speed) // 1000}G"
E           ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
```

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18305 added code to extract the `speed_gbps`:
```
        # Convert the speed to gbps format
        speed_gbps = f"{int(speed) // 1000}G"
        if speed_gbps not in SUPPORTED_SPEEDS:
```

However `intf_status` contains all ports (operationally up and down) and the ports that are down won't have a speed in STATE_DB, hence the error.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run `test_intf_fec.py::test_verify_fec_stats_counters`

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Test should pass but it's failing

linkedPullRequests.title: `test_intf_fec.py` skip ports that are link down
linkedPullRequests.author: arista-nwolfe
linkedPullRequests.body:
`test_verify_fec_stats_counters` iterates over all ports in `intf_status` (up and down)
A down port is going to return an empty string for it's speed from STATE_DB.
If we try to cast that into an int we'll get the following error:
```
        for intf in intf_status:
            intf_name = intf['iface']
            speed = duthost.get_speed(intf_name)
            # Convert the speed to gbps format
>           speed_gbps = f"{int(speed) // 1000}G"
E           ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
```

Fixes #20104
